reviews.title: CAO PHƯƠNG CHI · IELTS 49 · W07 · Đề 1
reviews.overall: Em đã xác định đúng số ô tô được sản xuất, viết đủ bốn đoạn và nêu đúng việc Thailand dẫn đầu ở cả ba năm. Tuy nhiên, hai đoạn Detail lặp lại số liệu Argentina trong khi chưa trình bày diễn biến của Australia và mức giảm của Thailand sau năm 2006. Em cũng gán 341 268 xe của Australia cho Argentina, và đưa mức 466 089 của năm 2009 vào giai đoạn kết thúc năm 2006. Cô yêu cầu em đối chiếu lại từng nước với từng năm, chia dữ liệu rõ hơn và soát các mệnh đề còn thiếu động từ đúng dạng.
reviews.dataGrouping: Em mở Detail 1 bằng Thailand rồi nói đến Argentina; Detail 2 lại tiếp tục nói về Argentina. Cách này khiến mốc 2003 của Argentina lặp lại, còn Australia không có số liệu trong Detail và Thailand không được mô tả ở năm 2009. Em có thể chia theo giai đoạn 2003–2006 và 2006–2009 để ba nước đều được so sánh ở các mốc quan trọng.

reviews.originalEssay:
The table compares the number of cars manufactured in Argentina, Australia and Thailand in 2003, 2006 and 2009.

Overall, car production in Argentina increased throughout the period, while Australia continuously decreasing and Thailand produced the most cars in all years.

To elaborate, in 2003, 735 852 cars were produced in Thailand, with a significant growth to 1 162 356 in 2006, marking the highest point of the entire table. The figures for Argentina also went up, from around 235 088 to 466 089 cars for the same period time.

Regarding categories with lower data, the number of cars produced in Argentina started at 235 088 cars in 2003, after which it rising progressively to 341 268 cars in 2006. The most significant growth was seen in the figures for Argentina, from a 235 088 to 466 089 between 2003 and 2009. This number; however, was still below those of Thailand.

By contrast, the Australian figure fell further to 245,624, so the gap between Argentina and Australia widened substantially.

The two line charts show how many men and women were in prison in a European country from 1911 to 2001.

Overall, male prisoners outnumbered female prisoners throughout the period. The male population fell initially before rising sharply, especially between 1971 and 1981. The female population dropped to a low in 1941, fluctuated thereafter and ended below its starting level.

In 1911, there were about 18,000 male prisoners, and this figure remained almost unchanged in 1921 before falling to roughly 10,000 in 1931. It then recovered to around 20,000 in 1961 and dipped slightly to about 19,000 in 1971. A sharp rise followed, taking the figure to approximately 39,000 in 1981 and then to about 46,000 in 2001, its highest point.

By contrast, the female prison population was far smaller, at approximately 3,200 in 1911. It declined to around 500 in 1941, then climbed to roughly 1,500 in 1961. After falling again to about 700 in 1971, it rose to around 1,900 by 2001, still well below the male figure.

reviews.originalEssay:
The line graph shows the amount of chicken, beef, lamb and fish eaten by people in a European country between 1979 and 2004.

Overall, chicken consumption increased over the period, while the beef, lamb and fish went down. Chicken became the most popular type of meat. And fish remained the least popular.

In 1979, beef was the most popular food, however, its consumption dropped over the years. On the other hand, the amount of chicken consumed went up. In 1989, chicken overtook beef and became the most popular meat in this country.

Regarding categories with lower data, lamb and fish both experienced a decreased trend between 1979 and 2004. The amount of lamb consumed dropped significantly over the 25 year period. Fish consumption started at a lower level and decreased. As a result, fish remained the least popular choice all types throughout the same period.

reviews.suggestedRevision:
The line graph compares weekly consumption of chicken, beef, lamb and fish in a European country from 1979 to 2004, measured in grams per person.

Overall, chicken consumption rose substantially and overtook that of beef around 1989, becoming the highest by 2004. By contrast, beef and lamb consumption fell markedly, while fish declined only slightly and remained the least consumed throughout.

In 1979, people consumed about 220 grams of beef per person per week, compared with 140 grams of chicken. Beef reached a peak of roughly 240 grams in the early 1980s before falling, with fluctuations, to about 110 grams in 2004. Chicken consumption also fluctuated slightly but rose overall, surpassing that of beef around 1989 and finishing at approximately 250 grams.

Lamb consumption began at about 150 grams per person per week and generally declined to roughly 55 grams by 2004, despite minor recoveries along the way. The figure for fish was far lower, at around 60 grams in 1979. It stayed below all three meat categories and edged down to about 35 grams at the end of the period.

reviews.suggestedRevision:
The table compares the proportions of residents aged 65 or above in Canada, Germany and the UK in 1988 and 2000, with projections for 2030.

Overall, the share of older residents rose in each country between 1988 and 2000 and is forecast to climb further by 2030. Germany records the highest proportions in all three years, whereas the UK has the lowest.

In 1988, 20.35% of Germans were at least 65 years old, compared with 16.45% in Canada and 14.25% in the UK. By 2000, the German figure had increased to 25.53%, while Canada's had reached 20.65%. The UK recorded a much smaller rise, of just 0.55 percentage points, to 14.80%.

By 2030, Germany's proportion is projected to reach 30.65%, remaining the highest of the three. The corresponding figure for Canada is expected to rise to 26.35%, keeping it between Germany and the UK. The British share is forecast to reach 20.45%, an increase of 5.65 percentage points from 2000, but it will still be the lowest.
